answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing and stated: (1) the tester's evidence.not_run_teeth is set only when verdict is RED and every failing tooth printed UNRAN (device.py:839-842, unran_only), so a proof with one UNRAN tooth and one real red carries no not_run_teeth and the baseline still refuses, which is correct. (2) A tooth UNRAN at HEAD stays out of every reversion reading; if a revert made it run, it could only add a green, never fake a red. (3) The hollow's per-file reading stays a dict of file -> list of redded teeth, because clearance.hollow_lacks (clearance.py:757-840) reads any non-list value as unreadable. So the unread teeth must NOT be written as a key inside evidence.hollow[tid]; they go to a sibling evidence key.
answers.builder_check: Questions a Haiku builder would need answered, now answered here. Where is the baseline? hollow.py run_all() and the `missing` computation just after it (about lines 1150-1216 at 2026-11-23); run_all must keep each proof's not_run_teeth from record['evidence']. What is subtracted? declared_teeth[rel] minus baseline green minus not_run[rel]; the declared set used by later readings drops not_run[rel] too. Where do the unread teeth land? evidence['hollow_not_run'][tid] = {proof_rel: sorted(teeth)} beside evidence['hollow'], through the same store write the seal already uses; never inside evidence['hollow'][tid]. What does the all-UNRAN refusal say? HollowUnmeasurable naming the proof, the teeth, and 'not run on this host'. What is the UNRAN line format? Whatever device.py's unran_only parses; the proof fixture should print a tooth the same way an existing host-bound proof does (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/proofs/test_a_pulse_owns_no_console_on_windows.py tooth 1). Proof timeout: keep under 300s, one scratch repo per clause.
